questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four core questions pipeline reporting answers?
options: Is pipeline moving fast enough through stages?
What deals are at risk of stalling or missing close date?
What is the company's total headcount?
questions.explain: Headcount has nothing to do with pipeline health. The four core questions are: how much is open, is it enough, is it moving, and what's at risk.

questions.q: What's the correct filter to build a report of only open pipeline from an Opportunities report type?
options: Stage not in (Closed Won, Closed Lost)
No filter is needed; all opportunities are open by default
questions.explain: Excluding both closed-won and closed-lost stages leaves exactly the open opportunities that make up the active pipeline.

questions.q: Why would a plain pipeline-by-stage report miss a deal that's been stuck in Negotiation for 90 days?
options: Stuck deals are automatically excluded from reports
A stage total only shows the aggregate amount in that stage, not how long any individual deal has been there
Salesforce deletes opportunities after 90 days in one stage
Negotiation-stage deals can't be reported on at all
questions.explain: A stage total just sums amounts — it can't distinguish a 90-day-old stuck deal from one that arrived yesterday. Days in current stage is the field that surfaces that distinction.

questions.q: Which field would you add a filter on to catch deals that have been sitting at the same stage too long?
questions.explain: Days in current stage is the standard Opportunity field built specifically to measure how long a deal has stayed at its current stage, making it the right filter for catching stuck deals.

questions.q: Which widget type best represents pipeline by stage, visualizing the expected drop-off between stages?
questions.explain: A funnel chart is designed to show a sequence that narrows at each step — exactly the shape of a pipeline moving from earlier to later stages.
